data.answer:
The best patent-scope classifier in the 2024 study was the **multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier**, with an **F1 score of 0.780** for predicting “broader” versus “not broader”, using first and all claims.[1] F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall—not the percentage of predictions classified correctly.[2]

The three-way MLP classifier ultimately used for the main analysis—“narrower”, “similar” or “broader”—had an F1 score of **0.772**.[3]

citations.quote: | First & All | Broader, Not Broader | MLP Classifier | 0.780 |

claims.text: The 2024 study's best patent-scope classifier was the MLP classifier, scoring 0.780 on F1 for broader versus not broader using first and all claims.

citations.quote: F1 - The harmonic mean of Precision and Recall.
Accuracy - The fraction of predictions the modelling correctly predicted

claims.text: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, rather than the percentage of predictions classified correctly.

citations.quote: | First & All | Narrower, Similar, Broader | MLP Classifier | 0.772 |
Ultimately, Narrower v. Similar v. Broader (with "scope3" as the target variable) was deployed to produce the data used in the descriptive and regression analyses in the main text.

claims.text: The three-way MLP classifier used for the main analysis classified patents as narrower, similar or broader and scored 0.772 on F1.
